presentation.label: Headphones as a third output
presentation.summary: Turn the headphone jack into a third assignable output pair and pick each track's outputs with CUE + LEVEL.
presentation.overview: Adds ROUTED to PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO > CUE CFG, beside NORMAL and STUDIO. In ROUTED, LEVEL sets a track's level and CUE + LEVEL chooses where it plays: MAIN, CUE or PHONES as stereo pairs in any combination, or a single mono jack of the six (track L+R summed at half each, so a centred sound keeps its level). The choice is stored in the Part, so it survives source and page resets, Part reload and project save. The MIXER's MIX knob becomes the PHONES output level. Inputs A/B and C/D keep their stock DIR routing to MAIN.
highlights: Three stereo output pairs: MAIN, CUE and the headphone jack.
Per track: any combination of MAIN, CUE and PHONES, or one mono jack (MAIN L/R, CUE L/R, PHONES L/R).
Routing lives in the Part: SRC page resets and track clears leave it alone.
With MASTER TRACK on, tracks routed to MAIN feed the master and track 8's destination picks where the master plays.
usage: PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO: select CUE CFG ROUTED and press YES.
On a track, hold CUE and turn LEVEL to choose its outputs; the LEV box shows the destination.
In the MIXER, MIX sets the PHONES output level. Choose NORMAL or STUDIO again to return to stock behaviour.

limitations: Development build: nothing has been built, run in the emulator or tested on hardware yet.
Changes core 0's mixdown on the DSP; modules that read or change the gain path or the output ring may conflict and are not yet declared.

access.location: PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO > CUE CFG > ROUTED; then CUE + LEVEL on any audio track.
steps: Include Phones Routing in your build.
Press PROJ (MKII) and open CONTROL > AUDIO. Move to CUE CFG, select ROUTED and press YES.
Select an audio track, hold CUE and turn LEVEL to pick its outputs.
